texts: how to put air in bike tire with hand pump here is a simple stepbystep guide to inflating your bicycle tires using a hand pump you will need a bicycle hand pump the valve type must match your tire valve your bicycle optional but recommended a separate tire pressure gauge stepbystep instructions 1 identify your valve type first look at the valve on your tire there are two main types schrader valve looks like a car tire valve a cylindrical metal stem with a small pin in the center presta valve taller and thinner with threads at the top and a small locking nut the small brass nut at the top must be unscrewed counterclockwise before inflating you will hear a slight hiss of air escaping this is normal 2 prepare the pump most modern pumps have a dualhead or smart valve heres how to use them for dualhead valves flip the lever or collar to match your valve type usually marked for smart valves simply press the valve head directly onto the valve the internal mechanism will automatically adapt if your pump has separate heads for each valve type attach the correct one 3 remove the valve cap unscrew the small plastic or metal cap from the valve and set it aside 4 connect the pump head for schrader valves simply press the pump head firmly and vertically onto the valve flip the lever on the pump head upwards to lock it in place this will clamp it for presta valves ensure the valve tip is unscrewed press the pump head on then flip the lever to lock it you may need to open a small lever on the pump head first before pressing it on 5 inflate the tire hold the pump head steady with one hand to prevent it from bending the valve pump the handle up and down with your other hand using a hand pump requires more strokes than a floor pump you will feel resistance as the tire inflates 6 checking tire pressure if your pump has a builtin pressure gauge stop inflating periodically to check the tire pressure in pounds per square inch if the gauge doesnt show a reading youll need to temporarily remove the pump and use a separate pressure gauge to measure the pressure the correct tire pressure range is printed on the side of the tire do not exceed the maximum psi value listed 7 removing the pump important flip the lever on the pump head downwards to unlock it pull the pump head straight off the valve stem you may hear a brief hiss this is just air escaping from the pump hose not a tire leak 8 securing the valve stem for presta valves tighten the small brass nut on the tip of the valve stem clockwise until its snug do not overtighten for all valve types replace the dust cap to prevent dirt from entering while not crucial for maintaining tire pressure it protects the valve stem quick troubleshooting tips air leaking while pumping you havent securely locked the lever on the pump head or the pump head isnt fully seated on the valve stem remove and reattach securely pump feels stuck or wont inflate the pump head may not be compatible with your valve type doublecheck the settings pumping is very difficult highpressure tires stand over the bike and use your body weight to increase leverage take breaks if needed pro tip for routine maintenance check your tire pressure every 12 weeks properly inflated tires roll easier prevent flats and make your ride safer and more comfortable for an easier way to inflate your bike tires consider using an electric tire inflator

eu to invest in brazil eu expected to announce investments in five mining companies operating in brazil in march pedro lovisi belo horizonte the brazilian government expects that by the end of march investors linked to the european union will announce investments in five mining companies operating in brazil the announcement is part of the interest of the president of the european commission ursula von der leyen in signing an agreement with brazil to secure the supply of critical minerals to europe according to ana paula repezza business director at apex brasil the brazilian trade and investment promotion agency european interest is initially focused on companies producing rare earths nickel lithium and manganese all essential for the manufacture of electric vehicles the eus main tool to decarbonize the transport sector the announcement is expected to take place on march 24 during an apex forum on investments involving brazil and the european bloc repezza declined to name which companies are expected to receive the investments as reported by folha one of these companies is viridis which is listed on the sydney stock exchange but has a brazilian fund as its main shareholder the company plans to extract rare earth elements in southern minas gerais starting in 2028 and is already holding frequent talks with european investors for example the french governments export bank is responsible for half of the debt contracted by the company to advance its project investments may also be directed to brazilian nickel which plans to operate in the state of piau and to amg lithium which already produces lithium in minas gerais both companies have recently participated in events organized by apex with european investors amg lithium in turn already operates a lithium processing plant in germany and in december received 36 million from a german government fund to expand its operations in the country repezza says that in all cases the european union is interested in having the processing and refining of these minerals carried out in brazil a position also defended by president luiz incio lula da silva there are no legal requirements mandating this however according to her such demands come from the market itself it makes sense for the eu to support and invest in the processing of critical minerals in brazil because the entire extraction and processing chain consumes a large amount of energy and brazil has the cleanest electricity matrix in the world and therefore the lowest carbon footprint repezza said negotiations between brazil and the european union follow a different path from the strategy adopted by the united states on critical minerals when dealing with foreign governments us authorities usually negotiate contracts and terms that guarantee supply and priority access to critical minerals for the country as folha has reported in some cases americans also choose to contact mining companies directly in the european case government signed on saturday 17 and its legal revision was approved by the european parliament on wednesday 21 von der leyen highlighted the eus interest in brazilian minerals during a speech celebrating the frequency response this exchange happens in a fraction of a second and is completely invisible to the driver the vehicles immobilizer control unit receives the signal and compares it with the authorized codes stored in its memory if the received code matches one of the stored entries the system allows the engine control module to enable fuel injection and ignition if the code is incorrect or missing the immobilizer remains active preventing the car from starting even if the mechanical part of the key fits the ignition the precision of this radio communication is crucial the signal strength frequency and timing must align perfectly for successful authentication any interference damaged antenna or faulty chip can disrupt this process leading to starting problems or warning lights a little too outside i mehek moved to a new place because i needed silence not peace i wasnt delusional enough to want that peace is for people who believe that they still have hope i just wanted the noise to stop the questions the looks the way people tilted their heads when they hear separated instead of married the way grief held on to me like second skin the grief of loosing my old self my old life my old voice that used to laugh without efforts so i left i left my family my marriage the city i left everything behind and carried my grief and two suitcases with me thats how i found the house it had a massive kitchen straight out of an old indian ancestral home all with heavy counters deep sinks cupboards that smelt faintly of wood and spices it had five bedrooms a hall so wide my footsteps should have echoed but it didnt there was a backyard fenced and overgrown but strangely still the rent was absurdly low cheaper than a one bedroom hall kitchen in the midst of the city i was intrigued i asked why the broker vijaybhai gave a fake smile and said its a little too outside that should have been my first red flag but i was desperate to find an accommodation that i could afford i had some savings i was not broke but not completely safe either i didnt have a job or a plan just grief sitting on my shoulders the house was the only thing that made financial sense the day i moved in i noticed something unnerving i had not bothered to pay attention before there was no dust not the recently cleaned kinds the never touched kinds no spider no webs no dirt in the corners the furniture looked old but immaculate like it has been waiting rather than abandoned that night i noticed the mirrors were a bit off my reflection lagged just a fraction a blink too late like the glass needed a moment to reflect me i laughed it off i guess trauma does that to you it makes you dramatic and suspicious of your own senses then i noticed the sound actually the lack of it there were no birds chirping no dogs barking no distant traffic hum no horns of vehicles passing by when i shut the main gate the world switched off completely even my footsteps didnt sound right no echoes no creaks an empty house should respond to you this one swallowed me whole i froze i told myself this is what you wanted silence the house never felt like home it felt like company not warm not hostile just present like someone sitting quietly beside you not speaking but never leaving yet it gave me everything i needed water ran endlessly electricity never flickered never ran out of gas summer didnt feel hot the house stayed mildly cold the kind that seeps into your bones i had always felt a little too chilly in my old life as well the house never got dirty once i left the kitchen in a mess on purpose i left the dishes in the sink over night spilled flour on the counter slept without sweeping the floor by morning everything was clean not scrubbed and rearranged but like someone had hit a reset button like the mess never ever happened it constantly kept me uneasy i let the feeling live like a roommate i stayed where else would i go the kitchen was too perfect to waste i started filming cooking videos just me my veiny hands the cold counters and the comforting clink of steel utensils people loved it and called it aesthetic hauntedcoreso calming it feels unreal some comments joked about ghosts subscribers grew money trickled in someone suggested a cloud kitchen another asked if the house was available for stays they said they would pay for the experience people drove in from the city to pick up food some asked if they could just come in and sit just for a bit soon the house wasnt just mine it became famous i was offered help with the licences staff marketing etc renovations happened without any chaos workers came did their job and left quietly no dust or debris rooms were ready before timelines the house was turned into a boutique hotel the rooms reset themselves the beds made themselves the bathrooms were always clean and dry no rats or insects ever infested there was never a decay no birds ever nested on the roof never was there a stray cat found the house managed itself i ran a restaurant mehek from the backyard it was fully booked months in advance i never had to hire cleaners or the kitchen staff the kitchen cleaned itself ingredients arrived exactly when i needed them the customers didnt mind waiting as they would get to sit there longer wafting in the mehek of the food the guests loved it they spoke in whispers without being told to some said they slept better than they had in years some said they cried for no reason one specific guest abhi asked an intriguing question is this house for people who have lost something i didnt answer i didnt know anything about the house i was unsettled and uneasy but comfortably so i know it doesnt make sense i guess grief distorts your perception at night i walked the corridors barefoot the floors were always warm soft and comfortable as if walking on leather sometimes i caught my reflection in the dark windows standing still even after i moved the question abhi had asked still loomed in my head i did some digging but found no photographs of previous owners no records no stories the house existed in paperwork as a structure not a home no one knew anything about its past one evening while reviewing bookings i realised something that made my chest tighten every long term guest had come here after a rupture a divorce a death a scandal or a disappearance no one arrived whole and happy the silence felt addictive and the mehek of the food intoxicating i started sleeping badly many times i would wake up suddenly and feel a heaviness on my chest my body unable to move sleep paralysis as they call it dreams became vivid rooms extending endlessly corridors rearranging behind me doors appearing where there were none before guests began extending their stay some stopped answering the calls from their family one woman madhvi missed her flight and didnt appear to be bothered at all another man yash asked if he could help the house somehow i asked what he meant he smiled and replied it already helps us many times i thought about leaving but the idea always felt exhausting because every time i stepped outside the main gate the air changed sound rushed back in violently horns birds animals people life and with it grief crushing heavy as if something compressing my chest and i felt unable to breathe when i stayed inside the grief sat across the room instead silent watching and bearable i stopped leaving i stopped missing my old life the old me i finally embraced it completely the silence i wanted was here i stopped dreaming eventually now sometimes when i walk past the mirrors my reflection doesnt lag it smiles before i do and last night while locking up the kitchen i heard something for the first time since a moved in nothing from the outside but from the house itself a quiet satisfied sigh like a person that finally knows i cant go anywhere i cant leave

robert friedland why we need to mine 10000 years of copper in 18 years original article physics vs economics why the green transition and the ai revolution are about to hit a geological wall if you gathered every ounce of copper mined since a human first banged a rock against a greenstreaked cave wall in 8000 bc you would have a pile weighing roughly 700 million tonnes it took us ten millennia to dig that much metal out of the earth according to mining billionaire robert friedland we have about 18 years to do it all over again in a recent address that has sent ripples of quiet panic through the commodities sector the ivanhoe mines founder laid out a mathematical reality that no amount of political optimism can solve friedlands thesis is stark even if we abandon the green transition tomorrow no more teslas no more wind farms no more netzero pledges the world still faces a catastrophic shortfall the core of the problem isnt the green dream its the mundane reality of standard economic growth we currently consume about 30 million tonnes of copper annually with a paltry 4 million tonnes coming from recycling friedland points out that simply maintaining a 3 global gdp growth rate requires us to duplicate the entire history of copper mining in less than two decades that figure assumes a businessasusual world running on oil and gas it does not account for the electrification of the global economy the retooling of power grids or the explosive energy demands of the ai revolution when you layer those factors on top the demand curve goes vertical while the public focus has been on electric vehicles a quieter more voracious beast has entered the market the hyperscale data center friedlands recent warnings highlight that the physical infrastructure needed to support artificial intelligence is vastly more copperintensive than previous tech cycles a standard data center is heavy on metal but aiready facilities require up to three times the copper for highdensity cooling systems and massive power distribution units we arent just asking the grid to work harder we are asking it to carry loads it was never designed to bear furthermore the narrative has shifted from purely environmental to existential in a darkening geopolitical climate copper has graduated from an industrial input to a national security asset modern warfare is wired warfare from guidance systems in ballistics to the complex circuitry of drones rearmament consumes base metals at a staggering rate as friedland bluntly noted when a gun is pointed at you you need copper to shoot back this realization is pushing nations from a justintime supply chain efficiency to a justincase hoarding mentality removing critical inventory from the open market the most sobering aspect of this crunch is the timeline in the software world a shortage is fixed with code in the mining world it is fixed with geology and permits it currently takes approximately 15 to 20 years to take a copper deposit from discovery to production we are effectively trying to meet 2030 deadlines with mines that should have been started in 2010 to make matters worse we are running out of the easy stuff the average grade of copper ore has plummeted by roughly 40 since the early 1990s miners today must move crush and process nearly twice the amount of rock to extract the same amount of metal as their predecessors this drives up energy costs and capital intensity pushing the incentive price the price at which it makes sense to build a new mine well above current market rates friedland suggests we may need to see copper stabilize at 15000 per tonne to spur the necessary massivescale development a figure significantly higher than the 900011000 range seen in recent volatility the world is facing a collision between the laws of physics and the laws of economics we have built a global roadmap for the future that relies entirely on a metal we are not digging up fast enough for investors and policymakers alike the message is clear the era of cheap abundant copper is over and the race to secure the physical building blocks of the 21st century has only just begun sources miningcom friedland footsteps should have echoed but it didnt there was a backyard fenced and overgrown but strangely still the rent was absurdly low cheaper than a one bedroom hall kitchen in the midst of the city i was intrigued i asked why the broker vijaybhai gave a fake smile and said its a little too outside that should have been my first red flag but i was desperate to find an accommodation that i could afford in i noticed something unnerving i had not bothered to pay attention before there was no dust not the recently cleaned kinds the never touched kinds no spider no webs no dirt in the corners the furniture looked old but immaculate like it has been waiting rather than abandoned that night i noticed the mirrors were a bit off my reflection lagged just a fraction a blink too late like the glass needed a moment to reflect me i laughed it off i guess trauma does that to you it makes you dramatic and suspicious of your own senses then i noticed the sound actually the lack of it there were no birds chirping no dogs barking no distant traffic hum no horns of vehicles passing by when i shut the main gate the world switched off completely even my footsteps didnt sound right no echoes no creaks an empty house should respond to you this one swallowed me whole i froze i told myself this is what you wanted silence the house never felt like home it felt like company not warm not hostile just present like someone sitting quietly beside you not speaking but never leaving yet it gave me everything i needed water ran endlessly electricity never flickered never ran out of gas summer didnt feel hot the house stayed mildly cold the kind that seeps into your bones i had always felt a little too chilly in my old life as well the house never got dirty once i left the kitchen in a mess on purpose i left the dishes in the sink over night spilled flour on the counter slept without sweeping the floor by morning everything was clean not scrubbed and rearranged but like someone had hit a reset button like the mess never ever happened it constantly kept me uneasy i let the feeling live like a roommate i stayed where else would i go the kitchen was too perfect to waste i started filming cooking videos just me my veiny hands the cold counters and the comforting clink of steel utensils people loved it and called it aesthetic hauntedcoreso calming it feels unreal some comments joked about ghosts subscribers grew money trickled in someone suggested a cloud kitchen another asked if the house was available for stays they said they would pay for the experience people drove in from the city to pick up food some asked if they could just come in and sit just for a bit soon the house wasnt just mine it became famous i was offered help with the licences staff marketing etc renovations happened without any chaos workers came did their job and left quietly no dust or debris rooms were ready before timelines the house was turned into a boutique hotel the rooms reset the house managed itself i ran a restaurant mehek from the backyard it was fully booked months in advance i never had to hire cleaners or the kitchen staff the kitchen cleaned itself ingredients arrived exactly when i needed them the customers didnt mind waiting as they would get to sit there longer wafting in the mehek of the food the guests loved it they spoke in whispers without being told to some said they slept better than they had in years some said they cried for no reason one specific guest abhi asked an intriguing question is this house for people who have lost something i didnt answer i didnt know anything about the house i was unsettled and uneasy but comfortably so i know it doesnt make sense i guess grief distorts your perception at night i walked the corridors barefoot the floors were always warm soft and comfortable as if walking on leather sometimes i caught my reflection in the dark windows standing still even after i moved the question abhi had asked still
